newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Wallenberg denies Nazi gold deals -paper.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Wallenberg denies Nazi gold deals -paper.

text.p: Swedish financer Jacob Wallenberg denied his family handled Nazi gold during World War Two, Metro newspaper reported on Saturday.
"There is no proof of any connection between what we worked with and property stolen from, for example, Jewish families," he told the paper.
Wallenberg, who has been nominated as new chief executive of bank S-E-Banken, invited a government commission looking into Nazi gold to search family archives, Metro said.
"We have nothing to hide," he was quoted as saying. "On the contrary. We try to help in any practical way possible."
He said the family had not found anything in the archives that supported allegations the Wallenbergs had traded with Nazi gold, the newspaper said.
"We ran commercial operations during the war, but so did others," he was quoted as saying.
"Regarding these accusations about trading with stolen gold, these are allegations. These allegations in the Swedish media have been turned into fact, which I find appalling."

Central and commercial banks in several European countries have been examining their archives after widespread accusations that Switzerland profited during the War from its dealings in gold and other assets belonging to Holocaust victims.
